title: CI token and secret policy: the task tokens, the token ceilings, the secret rules, the credential-to-lane map and the Gitea Actions facts at the pin

decision.note: Hostile-CI threat model, the validation and promotion lanes, and the CI runner's reach to Gitea: the Architect's design, revision 2, accepted by the Overseer at Q-02.1's completion (rulings R1 and R2); every act it names stays Owner-gated.

task_tokens.name: The job token (GITHUB_TOKEN and GITEA_TOKEN)
task_tokens.form: 40 hex characters minted per task, stored as a salted hash (G3)
task_tokens.delivery: In the task's secrets as GITHUB_TOKEN and GITEA_TOKEN and in the task context as token; the runner places it in the job environment (G3, A1).
task_tokens.authenticates_as: The Actions pseudo-user bound to the task (G3).
task_tokens.binding: The governance repository for its own task; any other repository only through a cross-repository grant, of which none exists (G4).
task_tokens.mode: restricted, under an all-none ceiling at the governance owner and repository and the workflow's permissions: {} (G4, ceilings below)
task_tokens.also_accepted_by: The v3 artifact route, as a Bearer fallback, for its own task (G8).
task_tokens.lifetime: One task: valid while the task is running or cancelling (G3).
task_tokens.notes: Public repositories stay readable by every job token whatever the ceiling (G4); the policy is that no public repository exists on the instance (disclosure ci-d1). The token is unusable from the job: it has no network path (policy/ci-runner-profile.json, reach).

task_tokens.name: The runtime JWT (gitea_runtime_token; expected in the job as ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN)
task_tokens.form: A JWT per task, HS256 with the instance's general token signing secret, scope Actions.Results:<run>:<job> plus cache write (G8)
task_tokens.delivery: In the task context as gitea_runtime_token (G8). Whether act_runner places it in the job environment is A1, verified at Q-02.2.1; the lane treats it as present either way.
task_tokens.authenticates_as: The task, at the artifact routes and act_runner's cache server (G8, A1).

effective_permission.artifact_routes: upload for its own job, but no path to them
effective_permission.cache_server: write, but the cache server is disabled

task_tokens.also_accepted_by: The v3 and v4 artifact routes and act_runner's cache server (G8, A1).
task_tokens.lifetime: One task, and the JWT is valid from issue for 1 h plus ENDLESS_TASK_TIMEOUT (4 h at the default) (G8).
task_tokens.notes: Inert: no network path, the artifact routes are denied by the filtering proxy (policy/ci-runner-profile.json, proxy), the cache server is disabled (runner configuration). Never recorded.

repositories.notes: The owner's ceiling governs (override false); the repository's own restricted mode and all-none ceiling make a later override change nothing.

workflow_permissions.notes: Checked on the source of record by tools/check_ci_policy.py.

ceilings.effective: min(none, none) = none on every unit of the governance repository; none on every other private repository (restricted-read clamp, then no cross-repository grant); read on every public repository of the instance, which no ceiling removes (G4).

secret_rules.rule: No Actions secret or variable exists at the governance repository, at its owner, at any other repository or owner of the instance, or instance-wide. G5 delivers every owner and repository secret to every task of a non-fork run and every variable, global ones included, to every task: an empty set is the only rule that keeps them out of jobs.
The runner host holds only cred-runner-token (root-owned on the CI guest, outside every mount) and the guest's own host keys; runner.envs and env_file are empty.

The registration token is a standing management-class secret in Gitea's database until reset (G2). The host-side Gitea-administration command resets it, reads it into memory, hands it to the dispatcher for one delivery over the management channel to the CI guest's register step, and resets it again immediately after a successful registration or a failed delivery. Never a file, a record, a log or the Owner's credential store.
The dispatcher's standing bot tokens, the site-administrator credential and the management key never enter the CI guest or a job: the dispatcher stages and dispatches from the host.

revocation.method: Always at CI-guest destroy: the administration command deletes the runner record (DELETE /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runners/{id}, owner-only); Gitea refuses the token at its next poll. An ephemeral runner is deleted by Gitea when its task ends.
Reset by the administration command after every registration and on any trigger; the reset is the revocation.
Ends with its task (Gitea); on suspected exposure the dispatcher cancels the run and recreates the CI guest.
Ends with its task at the artifact routes and expires with the JWT; on suspected exposure the dispatcher cancels the run and recreates the CI guest.
As the other bot tokens: rotated by gitea_roles.py rotate; the site administrator revokes it.

gitea_facts.fact: Actions is off on the host instance ([actions] ENABLED = false, observed) although the code default is on; it is also a per-repository unit; with the unit off globally or on the repository no workflow is detected, scoped workflows included. DEFAULT_ACTIONS_URL (github or self) names where the runner fetches uses: actions. SKIP_WORKFLOW_STRINGS skip push and pull-request runs.

The runner registers with a registration token scoped to the instance, an owner or one repository, which stays active after registration; the CLI and API return the latest active token; only the web settings' reset invalidates it. The runner then holds a persistent token (salted hash) and long-polls FetchTask and pushes Declare, UpdateTask and UpdateLog over Connect RPC under /api/actions/ (ping.v1.PingService and runner.v1.RunnerService only). Gitea never connects to a runner; a job never reports. An ephemeral runner is deleted when its task ends.

The job token is minted per task (20 random bytes as 40 hex characters, salted hash), delivered as GITHUB_TOKEN and GITEA_TOKEN and as the context's token, valid while the task is running or cancelling, and authenticates as the Actions pseudo-user with the task id.

A configurable token ceiling exists: per repository and per owner a mode (permissive: write on all units; restricted: read on Code, Packages and Releases), a per-unit MaxTokenPermissions and, per owner, AllowedCrossRepoIDs; a workflow's permissions: block is honoured and clamped; the default with nothing configured is permissive. Another repository is reachable only read-clamped through a cross-repository grant; every public repository is readable by every job token whatever the ceiling. Enforced for the API and git smart HTTP alike.

Every secret of the repository and of its owner is decrypted and delivered to every task of a run, except for fork pull requests (tokens only) unless the event is pull_request_target; called workflow jobs get only inherited or mapped secrets. Variables (instance-global, owner and repository) are delivered to every task, fork pull requests included.

Workflow definitions come from the pushed commit for push, the head ref for pull_request and the base branch for pull_request_target. A fork PR by an author without Actions write needs approval on every run until that author has a merged pull request; restricted users always.

Job results become commit statuses by the Actions pseudo-user with context '<workflow name, else file> / <job> (<event>)', scoped runs prefixed '<source repository>: ' (imitable); required checks match contexts by glob, not creators; posting a status needs write on Code.

Artifacts are uploaded by the job over /api/actions_pipeline/* (runtime JWT, or the job token as a Bearer fallback) and /twirp/github.actions.results.api.v1.ArtifactService/*, mounted only when Actions is enabled. The runtime JWT is in the task context, HS256, scoped to the run and job with cache write, valid 1 h plus ENDLESS_TASK_TIMEOUT. Logs are uploaded by the runner.

Listing or writing secrets and variables and every runner route need the repository owner or a site administrator; user-level secrets have no list route; workflow dispatch needs write on Actions, accepts any branch or tag as ref and returns the run id only with return_run_details=true; runs, jobs (with runner_id), logs and artifacts are readable with read on Actions; the run record exposes event, path, head_branch, head_sha, status, conclusion, actor and trigger_actor, not the dispatch inputs nor a scoped-run marker.

Scoped workflows exist: a source repository registered for an owner or the instance, per-workflow Required and status Patterns; content from the source repository's default branch; the run is created in the consuming repository with its ceiling, secrets and variables, only where the consumer's Actions unit is enabled; a consumer may opt out per workflow.

act_runner's config.yaml keys (labels and backends, envs and env_file, capacity, timeout, cache.enabled, container.privileged, network, options, valid_volumes, docker_host, force_pull, host.workdir_parent), register --ephemeral, the tokens and runtime URLs it places in the job environment, and NoSkipCheckout, as the Architect recalls them. act_runner is not pinned; nothing was fetched.

disclosures.text: The job token can read every public repository of the instance whatever the ceiling (G4); the policy is that no public repository exists, and the live check reports any that does. The token is in any case unusable from the job.

The registration token is a standing secret in Gitea's database between the reset steps; with the web-route automation it is live for minutes per provisioning; same-account processes can read it through the CLI at any time (decision 0013, point 6).

A container escape inside the CI guest reaches the runner, its token and the guest-loopback forward, hence the runner RPC (with the filtering proxy) or Gitea's whole HTTP listener (without it); it reaches nothing else. Its reward is a forged conclusion for its own tasks, bounded by the verifier and the CI guest's recreation.
The commit-status gate is forgeable by any holder of write on Code (G7); every such holder is a trusted-side custodian, and the promotion lane trusts the run record, not the status.
Same-account host processes can read every dispatcher-held token, the site-administrator credential and the registration token, and operate the forward (decision 0013, point 6).
Job-uploaded artifacts are not available: evidence is the runner-streamed log and the conclusion; reports as artifacts need a mediated job-to-Gitea path (Q-02.4).
A proposal that does not pass through the dispatcher gets no staged bundle and no dispatched validation: it fails closed.
The runtime JWT's presence in the job environment is assumed, not verified (A1); its validity (up to 4 h) outlives the task, which matters only if a path to the artifact routes is ever admitted.
The Gitea facts G1 to G10 are verified at source, not live; A1 is unverified. A failed live verification changes a mechanism, not a lane.
